title: The Soldier Who Kept Fighting WWII Until 1974
notes: Public-domain photographs of Onoda exist on Commons and are used. The 1944 photograph with his brother Shigeo is used twice deliberately.

The 1944 images are tagged public domain on Commons under Japanese law for photographs of that period. That status is well established but is a determination by Commons editors, not a statement from the rights holder; it is worth knowing if a claim is ever made.
Segments s25 to s27 concern the roughly thirty Filipino islanders killed by Onoda's group. The image is held still and empty on purpose. Do not substitute anything more dramatic.
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API and checked live.

LOW RESOLUTION: the period photographs are small files - surrender 1974 (37KB), Kozuka (55KB), Hiroo and Shigeo 1944 (78KB), Onoda young (104KB). Show them as cards at native size, never upscaled. Soft historical photographs read as authentic; upscaled ones read as fake.

v3: Onoda appears in the illustrations only as a lone soldier in a patched uniform and cap, rifle slung, seen from behind or in silhouette. Generate one reference of that figure and pass it with --ref. His real face appears only in the real photographs.
v3: no illustrated violence. The killings on Lubang are carried by stillness and empty places, never by staged scenes of shooting or of victims.
